title: Hardcoded gendered pronoun "him" in objected-state copy while the referee name is interpolated
evidence:
pub fn refcheck_state_objected(
  name name: String,
  first_name first_name: String,
) -> String {
  name
  <> " asked us not to contact him. All automated contact has stopped. This "
  <> "tells you nothing about "
  <> first_name
  <> ". You can ask "
  <> first_name
  <> " for another referee."
}
detail: The sentence interpolates an arbitrary referee name but hardcodes "him". A female referee renders "Sarah Daly asked us not to contact him." Test fixtures only use male "Colm Byrne", so tests never catch it.
recommended_fix: Drop the pronoun or make it gender-neutral, e.g. "asked us not to contact them" (or restructure: "{name} asked us to stop contact. All automated contact has stopped.")

title: Em-dash in implementer-authored unmoderated-flag sentence violates the RT copy ban
evidence: pub const refcheck_unmoderated_flag: String = "Unmoderated referee text — written by the referee, not reviewed by us."
detail: This string is implementer-authored (a §9.3 flag, not §4.2/§7.4/§10.3 verbatim copy). The repo-wide CI ban forbids em-dashes in user-facing copy; the ban's own example names this exact sentence as a violation.
recommended_fix: Replace the em-dash with a period or comma: "Unmoderated referee text. Written by the referee, not reviewed by us."

title: Em-dashes in implementer-authored timeline labels and the " — " batch joiner
evidence:
pub const refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed: String = "Applicant nudge — couldn't send"
TimelineLine(label <> " — " <> channels, at)
copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail
detail: Timeline labels are implementer-authored (the lens guard names them as such), yet they ship em-dashes: "Applicant nudge — couldn't send" plus every rendered batch line ("Invitation sent — email + SMS", "Reminder 1 sent — email + SMS", "Applicant nudge skipped — …"). Violates the RT CI em-dash ban.
recommended_fix: Use a plain separator: "Applicant nudge: couldn't send" and join channels with " + " only ("Invitation sent: email + SMS"), or an en-dash-free separator.

title: Spec-in-PR documents localStorage-persisted explainer dismissal that the code does not implement
location: client/src/model.gleam:316-321 + client/src/msg.gleam (RC4.2 additions) vs spec-rc4-2 (OWNS #3, Dev Notes)
evidence:
spec: "UserToggledRefcheckExplainer`, `UserDismissedRefcheckExplainer`; model: ... `refcheck_explainer_dismissed: Bool` (hydrated from localStorage `rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed`)" and "localStorage hydration mirrors the sweep-nudge pattern (`rt_dismissed_sweep_nudges_v2`, `client.gleam:5685`): key `rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed`"
code: "refcheck_auto_expanded: Set(String), ... refcheck_explainer_open: Bool" with only "UserToggledRefcheckExplainer -> #(Model(..model, refcheck_explainer_open: !model.refcheck_explainer_open), effect.none())"
detail: No localStorage read/write and no rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed key exist anywhere in the diff; the shipped state is a session bool reset on route change. The PR's own spec claims per-user persisted dismissal — the claimed "per-user dismissed state" is absent.
recommended_fix: Either implement localStorage hydration of the explainer state (write on toggle, hydrate in initial()), or update the spec to say the explainer is session-scoped only.

title: First-view auto-expand is consumed by the first detail landing even when there was nothing to expand
detail: The application id joins refcheck_auto_expanded on the first landing regardless of whether any completed rows existed. A reference that completes after the landlord's first visit will never auto-expand — the unseen summary renders collapsed on every later visit, contradicting "expanded by default on first view" (UX §7.4).
recommended_fix: Only mark refcheck_auto_expanded when summary_ids was non-empty (first landing with an actual summary to expand), so a later-completed row still auto-expands on the first view that carries it.

title: Unused copy constant refcheck_off_contacts_label is never referenced
evidence: pub const refcheck_off_contacts_label: String = "Referee details"
detail: view_off renders the heading, body, and three off_ref_block calls but never this constant; no other module references it. Either the "Referee details" section label is missing from the Off block (claimed by its own doc comment: "the referee details that follow") or it is dead code.
recommended_fix: Render the label above the three off_ref_block sections, or delete the constant if the §7.4 Off block carries no section label.

title: field_is_answered counts any object as answered, while render_value renders "Not answered" for content-less objects
detail: An object like {"from":"","to":""} or {"as_stated":false,"differs":"","stated":""} counts as answered for the partial line's m but renders "Not answered" in the same row's key-facts table — the two disagree on what answered means.
recommended_fix: Make field_is_answered mirror render_object_value (only count objects whose rendered value is not "Not answered"), or centralize answered-ness in one function used by both.

title: "Never red" test only pins the absence of two specific class tokens
evidence:
html |> string.contains("bg-score-red") |> should.be_false
html |> string.contains("text-score-red") |> should.be_false
detail: The test claims "no status ever renders red" but only asserts two class names are absent. All pill classes share the shape "bg-{color}/10 text-{color}"; a red pill using any other token (e.g. bg-red/10 text-red, bg-red-500) would pass the test while rendering red.
recommended_fix: Assert the complete class string of every pill in the matrix (all four allowed color pairs), or check that no rendered class contains "red".

title: Doc comment promises submitted_at is stamped on manual outcome, but no code path does that
evidence: shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam:462-463: "/// - `submitted_at` (RC4.2 additive, expand-only) is None until the referee\n///   submits the form (or a manual outcome is recorded) — the honest" — but the ONLY writer of the column is server/src/reference_checks/sql/complete_reference_call.sql:25 ("submitted_at    = now()," in the guarded 'contact_initiated' -> 'form_completed' submit). The guarded status-transition query server/src/reference_checks/sql/update_reference_call_status.sql SETs status/outcome/terminal_reason/next_attempt_at only (no submitted_at), and its only callers pass Skipped (trigger.gleam:570) and AwaitingCorrection (form_handler.gleam:1218) — no code path records a manual outcome at this sha.
detail: The new contract doc claims manual-outcome recording sets submitted_at; no such path exists. When RC4.3 wires the manual-record action through update_reference_call_status, the promised 'Reference received' timestamp will silently stay absent on manual_recorded terminals.
recommended_fix: Stamp submitted_at = now() in update_reference_call_status.sql when the target status is manual_recorded (or note this in the RC4.3 story so the documented semantics hold).

title: "Form opened" timeline line is pinned after the invitation batch even when the form opened after later batches — mini timeline renders out of chronological order
detail: form_opened_at is stamped on any live form GET (form_handler.gleam:159 `stamp_form_opened(db, token)`), the reminder email carries the link (messages.gleam:254 `form_url(ctx.base_url, ctx.form_token)` in build_reminder_email_html), and the sweep's due-select has no form-opened gate (UX §4.3: "suppresses the nudge email but not reminders"). A referee opening from the reminder-1 email at T+50h renders Invitation (T0) → Form opened (T+50h) → Nudge (T+24h) → Reminder 1 (T+48h): the inserted line's timestamp is later than the following lines, so the "what has happened so far" sequence is false.
recommended_fix: Insert the form-opened line at its chronological position — compare form_opened_at against each batch's `at` — or sort the assembled lines by timestamp before rendering.

title: relationship_other (referee's verbatim "Other" relationship text) is never rendered — key-facts shows bare "Other"
detail: Server always emits the key — result.gleam:173 `#("relationship_other", str_or_null(draft, "relationship_other")),` and questions.gleam:409-411 `#("relationship_other", json.string(other))` when the referee picks "other" — but the panel's comment's claim that it "renders with its parent 'Other' row" is false: relationship_to_applicant renders as the word "Other" and the 1-200 char explanation is dropped from the key-facts table.
recommended_fix: Render the companion text with the parent row (e.g. "Other — <text>") in view_parsed_summary, or add relationship_other as its own key-facts row.

title: status_timestamp's Partial/ManualRecorded branches can never fire — partial rows permanently render without a timestamp
detail: submitted_at is stamped only by complete_reference_call.sql (`submitted_at    = now(),`). sweep_terminal.sql — the production T+144h abandoned-draft terminal that writes status 'partial' — sets status/outcome/result/next_attempt_at but never submitted_at; update_reference_call_status.sql (manual_recorded) doesn't either. So Partial rows always hit `None -> None` and show no date, contradicting §7.4 "same layout as received" (pill + timestamp).
recommended_fix: Stamp `submitted_at = now()` in sweep_terminal.sql (and the RC4.3 manual-record path), or drop the Partial/ManualRecorded branches from status_timestamp.

title: submitted_at is never stamped for partial/manual_recorded rows — the status_timestamp arms for them can never fire, and the shared doc comment claims the opposite
evidence: shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam:463-464: "///   submits the form (or a manual outcome is recorded) — the honest" / "///   "Reference received" timestamp. Neither the attempts log nor the stored"; shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam:488: "/// referee submits (or a manual outcome is recorded); the panel's"; complete_reference_call.sql:25: "    submitted_at    = now()," (grep of terminalize_reference_call.sql, update_reference_call_status.sql, sweep_terminal.sql: zero matches for submitted_at); client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:445-452: "FormCompleted | ManualRecorded | Partial | Completed -> case call.submitted_at { Some(ts) -> Some(format.format_timestamp_short(timestamp: ts)) None -> None }"
detail: Only complete_reference_call.sql (form submit) writes submitted_at. The T+144h sweep terminal (sweep_terminal.sql -> partial/unreachable) and any future manual outcome never do, so Partial rows always arrive with "submitted_at":null and the client's Partial arm renders no timestamp — the §7.2 'status pill + timestamp' row pattern is broken for a reachable terminal state, and the false comment steers RC4.3's manual-outcome writer wrong.
recommended_fix: Stamp submitted_at = now() in sweep_terminal.sql and terminalize_reference_call.sql (manual paths), or correct the shared doc comment to say form-submission only; client already degrades safely.

title: Form-opened timeline <time datetime> carries raw Postgres ::text format whose colon-less offset is an invalid HTML datetime value
evidence: list_reference_calls_for_detail.sql:32: "  COALESCE(form_opened_at::text, '') AS form_opened_at,"; client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:568: "                attribute("datetime", line.at),"; client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:537-546: "case call.form_opened_at { Some(ts) -> ... TimelineLine(copy.refcheck_timeline_form_opened, ts) ... }" — timestamptz::text renders e.g. "2026-08-01 21:12:00+00" (offset without colon), which the HTML spec's valid-global-date-and-time grammar rejects (offset must be Z or ±hh:mm); attempt-log at values are RFC3339 (timestamp.to_rfc3339, sweep.gleam:180) so only the form-opened line is affected.
detail: The new form_opened_at wire value (Postgres ::text) is injected verbatim into the <time> datetime attribute; "+00"/"+01" style offsets are not valid HTML datetime offsets. Visible text is correct — only the machine-readable value is invalid.
recommended_fix: Normalize the timestamp server-side (e.g. to_char(...,'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SSOF')) or emit the RFC3339 form for datetime while keeping the display string.

title: Em-dash in implementer-authored unmoderated-flag sentence (RT CI ban on em-dashes in user-facing copy)
evidence: pub const refcheck_unmoderated_flag: String = "Unmoderated referee text — written by the referee, not reviewed by us."
detail: RT CI ban: no em-dashes in user-facing copy. This sentence is implementer-authored — the UX spec §9.3 mandates a display-time warning affordance but ships no wording (grep of ux-reference-checking-v1 for 'Unmoderated' returns nothing), and the shared lens brief names the unmoderated-flag sentence as a place where an added em-dash is a defect. Renders on every completed/partial summary carrying free text.
recommended_fix: Replace the em-dash: "Unmoderated referee text. Written by the referee, not reviewed by us."

title: Em-dash in implementer-authored timeline label "Applicant nudge — couldn't send"
evidence: pub const refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed: String = "Applicant nudge — couldn't send"
detail: RT CI ban: no em-dashes in user-facing copy. UX §7.6's timeline lines are 'Invitation sent — email + SMS', 'Form opened', 'Reminder 1 sent', 'Reminder 2 sent', 'Applicant asked to nudge', 'Closed — no reply' — no 'couldn't send' variant exists in any spec, and the lens brief names timeline labels as implementer-authored strings where an added em-dash is a defect. Rendered in the in-flight mini timeline.
recommended_fix: Drop the em-dash: "Applicant nudge couldn't send".

title: Key-facts word map keys on phantom wire value 'their_landlord'; real wire value 'landlord' renders raw in the landlord-facing table
evidence:
copy.gleam:750:    "their_landlord" -> "Their landlord"
questions.gleam:125:        #("landlord", form_copy.opt_their_landlord),
reference_panel.gleam:911:        Ok(Some(s)) -> copy.refcheck_choice_word(s)
(copy.gleam fallback:    _ -> value)
detail: The landlord-slot 'Their landlord' option stores wire value 'landlord' (questions.gleam:125, draft key relationship_to_applicant passed through verbatim by result.gleam's landlord_verification), but refcheck_choice_word maps 'their_landlord' — a value the server never emits — and has no 'landlord' key. A completed landlord reference with that answer renders the raw token 'landlord' in the key-facts table, violating §7.4 'Values rendered in words'. Test fixtures use the phantom 'their_landlord', masking the gap; the story spec's word-map total-match testing standard is unmet.
recommended_fix: Map "landlord" -> "Their landlord" in refcheck_choice_word and fix the panel-test fixtures to the real wire value.

title: Explainer 'per-user dismissed state' not implemented — session-scoped toggle replaces localStorage hydration
evidence:
story spec OWNS #3: "`UserToggledRefcheckExplainer`, `UserDismissedRefcheckExplainer`; model: ... `refcheck_explainer_dismissed: Bool` (hydrated from localStorage `rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed`)"; model.gleam:319:    refcheck_explainer_open: Bool,
msg.gleam:249:  UserToggledRefcheckExplainer
client.gleam:655:            refcheck_explainer_open: False,
client.gleam:3257:      Model(..model, refcheck_explainer_open: !model.refcheck_explainer_open),
detail: UX §7.3 chrome spec ('Collapsible explainer — collapsed by default, per-user dismissed state') and the story spec's OWNS #3 (UserDismissedRefcheckExplainer + localStorage key rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed) are not implemented: no UserDismissedRefcheckExplainer message and no localStorage key exist, and the toggle resets on every route change. Practical impact is nil since the explainer is collapsed by default and never auto-opens, hence note severity.
recommended_fix: Hydrate refcheck_explainer_dismissed from localStorage rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed per the story spec, or amend the story spec to record the session-scoped decision.

title: Character slot's 'answered {m} of {n}' counts free_text_signals — a field the character form never asks
evidence:
reference_panel.gleam:836-843:      "character_ref" -> [ "identity_confirmed", "relationship", "capacity", "known_duration", "character_statement", "would_stand_again", "free_text_signals", ]
result.gleam:210-218: "// AD-9 shape completeness (N1, Perkins r1): the character slot carries no optional free-text question, so the array is empty — but the field is present for RC4's uniform-read contract."
detail: answered_count totals slot_field_keys, so a character referee who answered all 6 real questions (partial state) renders 'answered 6 of 7 questions, then stopped' — n=7 includes free_text_signals, which the character form never sets (its free text is the required character_statement) and which is always [] per result.gleam. Landlord/employer forms do ask the optional free-text question, so only the character slot overcounts.
recommended_fix: Exclude "free_text_signals" from the character slot's field set (n = 6), or align all slots' n on the server's required_draft_keys sets.

title: Panel re-derives terminality client-side; its set already diverges from the server's (omits Completed) and hooks are ignored
detail: Server computes terminality as `!hooks.can_record_manual` (§8.2); the panel re-implements the rule and the sets already differ: `Completed` is terminal server-side but not in the panel's list, so a v2 voice-completed row would flip the sub-line to "in flight". Future status additions drift silently.
recommended_fix: Derive terminality from the server contract: `!call.hooks.can_record_manual` inside is_terminal (or add Completed to the case), keeping one stable rule per AR-RC13.

title: Em-dashes added in implementer-authored shipped strings (unmoderated flag + nudge timeline lines), violating the no-em-dash copy convention
evidence: client/src/copy.gleam:667: `pub const refcheck_unmoderated_flag: String = "Unmoderated referee text — written by the referee, not reviewed by us."`; client/src/copy.gleam:844: `pub const refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed: String = "Applicant nudge — couldn't send"`; client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:623: `copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail`. Architecture §9.3 specifies only a "display-time warning affordance" with no copy; UX §7.6 lists only "Applicant asked to nudge". Base develop copy.gleam ships zero em-dashes in strings (`git show develop:client/src/copy.gleam | grep '= ".*—'` → none).
detail: These three strings are implementer-authored (no spec copy exists for them), so their em-dashes are new violations of the RT no-em-dash rule. Spec-verbatim em-dashes elsewhere (in-flight sub-line, §7.5 signals, confidence line, §7.6 invite line) are fine.
recommended_fix: Reword without em-dash: "Unmoderated referee text, written by the referee and not reviewed by us"; join the nudge-skipped detail with a comma or colon instead of " — ".

title: Spec'd per-user explainer dismissed state (localStorage rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed) not implemented — session-scoped only
evidence: Spec OWNS #3 (in-chunk): "`refcheck_explainer_dismissed: Bool` (hydrated from localStorage `rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed`)" and Dev Notes: "localStorage hydration mirrors the sweep-nudge pattern (`rt_dismissed_sweep_nudges_v2`, `client.gleam:5685`): key `rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed`". Worktree: client/src/model.gleam:319 `refcheck_explainer_open: Bool,`; client/src/client.gleam:655 `refcheck_explainer_open: False,` (route-change reset); toggle at client.gleam:3257 `Model(..model, refcheck_explainer_open: !model.refcheck_explainer_open)` with `effect.none()`. `grep -rn rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed client/` → zero hits.
detail: UX §7.3 requires a "per-user dismissed state"; the shipped explainer resets to closed on every navigation with no localStorage read/write, so a dismissing landlord is re-shown the explainer on return. ACs don't pin persistence, hence note severity.
recommended_fix: Hydrate from and persist to localStorage key rt_refcheck_explainer_dismissed on the toggle (sweep-nudge pattern at client.gleam:5747), or drop the per-user claim from the spec.

title: reference_panel.gleam is 1263 lines — 3× the <400 view-module target, bundling view + JSON decoding + signal thresholds
evidence: `wc -l client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam` → 1263; next-largest component leaderboard_view.gleam is 804 lines. JSON/signal logic lives inside the view module: line 905 `fn render_value(key: String, value: Result(Dynamic, Nil)) -> String {`, 1047 `fn worth_knowing_signals(fraud_signals: Option(Dynamic)) -> List(String) {`, 1112 `fn signals_decoder() -> decode.Decoder(Signals) {`, 1213 `fn parsed_result_decoder() -> decode.Decoder(ParsedResult) {`, alongside view_* functions. AGENTS.md target: "<200 lines for logic modules, <400 lines for view modules".
detail: The component mixes the §7.4 view with result-JSON decoding, per-slot field registries, signal thresholds and word rendering. RC4.3/RC4.4 edits (actions menu, attempt-log export) land on the largest surface in the client, raising change cost.
recommended_fix: Extract the result-parsing half (parsed_result_decoder, signals_decoder, worth_knowing_signals, render_value family, slot_field_keys) into components/reference_result.gleam; keep the panel module view-only.

title: Mini-timeline list is unkeyed although rows use keyed.ul and the list grows as attempt batches arrive
evidence:
client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:553-555: `html.ul(
      [attribute("role", "list"), class("space-y-1.5")],
      list.map(lines, fn(line) {` — html.li children carry no key. Contrast the rows list, line 258: `keyed.ul(
    [attribute("role", "list"), class("divide-y divide-slate-100")],
    list.map(calls, fn(call) {
      #(call.reference_call_id, view_row(call, app, expanded))`. Codebase precedent: application_detail_audit_trail.gleam:54 uses `keyed.ul(` for its timeline.
detail: AGENTS.md requires keyed elements for dynamic lists with stable IDs. The timeline grows over a row's life (invite → nudge → reminders) and has a stable key available (batch `at` timestamp); unkeyed items invite Lustre DOM-reuse mismatches on refresh.
recommended_fix: Use keyed.ul with `#(line.at <> line.label, ...)` for the timeline lines, mirroring the rows list and the audit-trail component.

title: Panel's `is_terminal` re-derives the server terminal rule and omits `Completed`, contradicting its own comment and the server's canonical set
evidence: client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:112-124: "/// Terminal statuses per the migration's live-row exclusion set (A6: skipped is NOT terminal — it re-enables to queued). fn is_terminal(call: ReferenceCallDetail) -> Bool { case call.status { FormCompleted | Partial | Unreachable | Refused | Objected | ManualRecorded | Failed -> True _ -> False } }" — vs server/src/application/application_detail_handler.gleam:1089-1096 which includes "shared_reference_call.Completed -> True" in compute_hooks_decoded's terminal set, and supabase/migrations/20260731222000_create_reference_call.sql:140 "WHERE status NOT IN ('form_completed','unreachable','refused','objected','manual_recorded','failed','completed','partial')" — the migration's live-row exclusion set the comment claims to mirror contains 'completed'. The panel itself treats Completed as terminal everywhere else (status_pill:419 renders teal "received"; row_detail:517 routes Completed to view_completed).
detail: AR-RC13 drift: terminality is already on the wire via server-computed hooks.can_record_manual (!terminal), but the panel re-implements the status→terminal map and diverges on `Completed` — an all-completed panel would render the in-flight subline. Latent only (v2-reserved status never emitted by v1 servers), but the comment's claim of mirroring the migration set is false.
recommended_fix: Derive the subline's terminality from the server hook (`!call.hooks.can_record_manual`) instead of re-mapping statuses, or add `Completed` to the is_terminal case to match compute_hooks_decoded and the migration index.

title: Mini-timeline rows render unkeyed while the rows list in the same module uses keyed.ul
evidence: client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:553-555: "html.ul( [attribute("role", "list"), class("space-y-1.5")], list.map(lines, fn(line) {" — vs line 258: "keyed.ul( [attribute("role", "list"), class("divide-y divide-slate-100")], list.map(calls, fn(call) { #(call.reference_call_id, view_row(call, app, expanded)) })" — the timeline lines are a dynamic list (attempt batches grow over the row's life) with a stable natural key (the batch timestamp `at`), yet are diffed positionally.
detail: Violates the repo convention (AGENTS.md: "Keyed elements for all dynamic lists with stable IDs") and Lustre's keyed-ul practice for lists that grow; text-only content makes it harmless today, but RC4.4 attempt-log expansion would add per-line state on an unstable base.
recommended_fix: Switch the timeline to keyed.ul and key lines by their batch timestamp (`line.at`), mirroring the rows list's keyed.ul with reference_call_id.

title: reference_panel.gleam is 1263 lines — the largest component by ~57%, well past the <400-line view-module target
evidence: wc -l client/src/components/*.gleam: "1263 client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam" vs "804 client/src/components/leaderboard_view.gleam" (next largest) and the AGENTS.md target "Target: <200 lines for logic modules, <400 lines for view modules". The module bundles 12 state views, the timeline, the completed-summary renderer, and ~300 lines of payload decoders (parsed_result_decoder, signals_decoder, form_session_decoder, render_value family).

title: Em-dashes in implementer-authored mini-timeline nudge labels violate the em-dash ban
evidence: client/src/copy.gleam:844: `pub const refcheck_timeline_nudge_failed: String = "Applicant nudge — couldn't send"` and client/src/components/reference_panel.gleam:623: `copy.refcheck_timeline_nudge_skipped <> " — " <> skipped.detail` (renders "Applicant nudge skipped — {detail}"). title: refcheck_off_contacts_label export is unused anywhere
evidence: client/src/copy.gleam:567: `pub const refcheck_off_contacts_label: String = "Referee details"` — repo-wide grep (client/src, client/test, server, docs) finds no reference to `refcheck_off_contacts_label` outside this definition line.
